result.title: Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time
result.summary: Layer-local self-supervised objectives remove the backward pass between layers, but almost all still compute their loss over a batch of samples and are therefore local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), a spatially and temporally local learning rule for self-supervised representation learning from sequential input streams. The key idea is to instantiate a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and non-differentiated running population statistics, yielding a per-neuron online loss with bounded state. The objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis, and its gradient is a Hebbian update of the feedforward weights and an anti-Hebbian update of one lateral matrix per layer. The aim of the experiments is to show that the rule works in a small network, not to compete with backpropagation. On a class-chunked MNIST stream, a two-layer fully connected network trained with batch size one outperforms random features (96.48% versus 95.09% linear-probe accuracy) and classical SFA, and a variant that relaxes both locality constraints is comparable to supervised backpropagation. Because training and inference use the same computation, the network can keep learning from unlabeled data during inference without loss of accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TeReL：用时间相邻正样本与非可微的滑动总体统计量实例化 VICReg 式目标，得到逐神经元、状态有界的在线损失，使表示学习在空间与时间上同时局部化；在两层层全连接网络上以 batch size 1 从 MNIST 分块序列流训练，验证该规则可行并可在推理中继续学习。
AI.relevance_reason: 其层级局部加时间局部的在线目标与有界状态更新（前馈 Hebbian、侧向 anti-Hebbian）可能为 latent 推理状态的局部监督与测试时持续更新提供线索，但无多模态或推理实验，迁移可行性需核查。
